full_judgment:
10. The plaintiffs contended, inter alia, that the suit land was owned by Begraj Churuleya and R.O.R. khatian was recorded in his name. Accordingly, he proposed to sell the land to the plaintiff and the plaintiff accepted the proposal and a bainapatra was executed on 23.09.1963 and possession of the suit land was delivered in favour of the plaintiff. Due to non-execution of kabala and failure to register the same by Begraj Churuleya, the plaintiff and others filed Other Class Suit No.86 of 1974 for specific performance of contract. The suit was decreed on 27.11.1974 and pursuant to the said decree in Execution Case No.2 of 1976, the plaintiff got deed of sale on 14.07.1976 through court. The Government of Bangladesh and Deputy Director of special property Division of the Ministry of Industry filed other suit No.388 of 1975 against the plaintiff for setting aside the decree passed in Other Class Suit No.86 of 1974. The suit was dismissed on contest by judgment and decree dated 31.05.1979. The plaintiffs of that suit filed other Appeal No.206 of 1979 before the District Judge, Mymensingh against the decree, and the appeal was also disallowed on 07.04.1981. There are two parts of holding No.107 and the disputed land was situated in the southern part of that holding. There is a jute godown in the Northern part of holding No.107. Defendant No.1 is in possession of that godown as lessee under the Government. The Government published as auction notice in the Daily Ittefaq to sell the suit land and Defendant No.1 participated in the said auction and that was accepted by Defendant No.2 on 25.08.1981. The plot number, Khatian number and area of the land were not mentioned in that auction notice. Only holding No.107 was mentioned in that notice. The plaintiff was informed from the employee of Defendant No.1 that defendant No.1 will dispossess the plaintiff because the suit land is a part of holding No. 107. The plaintiff will suffer irreparable loss, if Defendant No.1 dispossesses the plaintiff in connivance with other defendants. Hence plaintiff filed the suit. 

 19. Mr. Neogi lastly also submits that it was decided in Other Class Suit No.388 of 1975 and other Class Appeal No.206 of 1979 that the suit land of the instant suit is different from the land claimed by the appellant and that finding is final and binding upon the parties of that suit and their successors in interest; but both the courts below dismissed the suit without considering that vital aspects of law which was reversed by the High Curt Division lawfully and as such the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. The predecessor of present respondents Firoja Begum mutated her name in S.A Khatian no.646 and paid rent regularly; Government acquired 13 decimals of land out of 25.50 decimals of land. from Firoja Khatum for Shombhugonj Sarak Bridge Project; vide L.A Case No.21/A(88-89); Firoja Begum filed Arbitration Case No.214 of 1989 in the Court of Arbitration Court, Mymensingh for proper compensation and she got the award of Tk.6,30,00/- by order dated 17.01.1999 and considering those aspects the original plaintiff has been recognized as tenant of the Government for the suit land; but both courts below dismissed the suit which was rightly reversed by the High Court Division.
